criteria.connection_begin: A refused or closed begin reports connection_failed with phase begin. The native failure is connection-flavored, the pool boundary owns connection errors, and transaction_failed stays reserved for failures inside an established transaction.
criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot separate these placements, or neither keeps the required contracts.
criteria.transaction_begin: A refused or closed begin reports transaction_failed with phase begin. The failing operation is transaction entry, the pool already proved its own connection at open, and callers handle one entry error.

begin_failure_error.instructions: Choose which error reports a natively refused or closed begin call on an open pool. Use common and topics.begin_failure_error.

criteria.opaque_random: The ID is fresh randomness minted per attempt. Nothing about pool identity, ordering, or attempt count leaks into diagnostics, and every report is trivially unique.
criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot separate these ID shapes, or neither keeps the required contracts.
criteria.structured_sequence: The ID derives deterministically from the pool resource identity plus a per-pool attempt counter. Operators correlate attempts to pools in logs, and tests assert exact IDs, while the value still carries no driver payload.

commit_unknown_id.instructions: Choose the transaction_id shape for commit_unknown reports. Use common and topics.commit_unknown_id.

criteria.bounded_drain: The drain runs under a fixed deadline; unsettled owners at expiry report transaction_failed with phase drain instead of committing. Commit latency stays capped even when a sublease never settles.
criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot separate these drain policies, or neither keeps the required contracts.
criteria.unbounded_drain: Commit waits however long existing subleases need; the native callback stays pending until the drain completes. No artificial deadline can abort running work, matching the owner scope contract where drains complete.

drain_bound.instructions: Choose whether the pre-commit drain waits unbounded or under a deadline. Use common and topics.drain_bound.

fixed_constraints: The catalogue binds sql::with_transaction<T> to the connection_failed, transaction_failed and commit_unknown errors, with phases on the first two and a transaction_id on the third. Its callback takes sql::transaction, returns sql::decision<T> and emits nothing; the decision variant holds exactly the commit<T> and rollback<T> record leaves, each carrying its value.

Measured Bun 1.4.2 behavior: begin resolves to the callback return value on commit and rejects with the identical thrown object on abort, so an identity-checked sentinel survives the round trip. A refused begin raises PostgresError ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_REFUSED; begin on a closed pool raises PostgresError ERR_POSTGRES_CONNECTION_CLOSED. Nested tx.begin rejects natively with a savepoint hint, and statements after a failed statement in the same transaction fail with 25P02. The tx handle calls with the same tagged-template shape as the pool client.

The owner scope contract admits one active transaction scope: nested with_transaction entry and escaped or stale handle use throw through invalid() as standard resource_state failures. Rollback is a private sentinel throw handled outside begin; commit returns only after the scope drains; a preserved primary standard failure outranks secondary cleanup failures; a native rejection after a commit decision reports commit_unknown and is never retried.

Transaction query operations reuse the I35 parameter validation, row decoding and native classification: only PostgresError classifies, foreign throws propagate to the generic fault path, and sanitized fields only (never message, detail, URL or credentials) reach diagnostics.
common.purpose: Advise the Can transaction implementation strictly from the evidence supplied here. Do not browse, implement, or explain. When candidates cannot be separated on the evidence, choose the marked uncertainty outcome.

begin_failure_error.facts: with_transaction emits both connection_failed and transaction_failed, each with a phase string. A refused or closed begin arrives as a connection-flavored PostgresError, yet the failing operation is transaction entry on an already-open pool whose own open succeeded. The phase value begin is available on either error.

commit_unknown_id.facts: commit_unknown carries one free string, transaction_id, and must stay safe for diagnostics: no driver payloads or credentials. The runtime knows the pool resource identity and can count attempts, or mint fresh randomness per attempt. Either shape survives the fault-proxy test, which only requires that the ID is present and safe.

drain_bound.facts: After the callback settles, its scope is marked closing and registered owners drain while the native begin callback stays pending; commit returns only after the drain. Existing subleases are allowed to finish. The suite must still exercise nonsettling owners under an external supervisor, so the drain policy must leave that behavior observable rather than masking it.
